clue.text: Lark about with half-hearted nobleman

parts.note: PEER with one of its two central Es removed

explanation.surface: A lord who can only half commit to a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' could be the bird, but the clue has no birds in it; here it is a spree.

clue.text: Secures shellfish I meant to add

parts.note: a postscript is what you write when you meant to add something

explanation.surface: A cook remembering the clams they forgot to put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I meant to add' is the voice of a letter-writer's afterthought, the classic postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to clamp a thing is to fix it firmly in place, to secure it.

clue.text: Best, by far, way to add colour?

definitions.meaning: read literally: putting in a shade, a tint

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic, hence the question mark: 'shade' as a tint of colour, not as shadow.

clue.text: Sticky thing, dealing with crime

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, a crime

explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: resin is the gummy substance that oozes from trees.

clue.text: Full coverage of planet circling towards moon

explanation.surface: An astronomer's report on a planet swinging round to face a moon.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is crosswordland's favourite moon, and Saturn's rings make 'circling' feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense of the phrase: saturation coverage leaves nothing untouched, full coverage.

clue.text: Chewed up list pet drops from mouth

explanation.surface: A dog has chewed up the list and dropped the soggy bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a verb for the pet letting go; it is a plural noun, drops of saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: spittle is saliva, the drops that fall from a mouth.

clue.text: Furiously sound horn to help arrest

parts.note: to nail a suspect is to catch them

explanation.surface: A driver leaning angrily on the horn to summon help with an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furiously' looks like an adverb for the horn-blowing, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to fight tooth and nail is to fight with every weapon, furiously.

clue.text: Top up her grace, getting smashed

indicators.note: Something smashed is broken into bits that can be put back in any order.

explanation.surface: A duchess keeps having her glass refilled until she is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top up' and 'smashed' conspire to suggest drinks; the definition works just as well for a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to recharge a battery, or a glass, is to top it up.

clue.text: Highlight missing the first strand of hair

indicators.note: A word missing its first letter has lost its opening S.

parts.note: to highlight a point is to stress it

explanation.surface: A hairdresser has missed the first strand when doing highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: Highlights are a salon treatment, so 'Highlight' looks like part of the hair scene; here it means emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a tress is a lock or strand of hair.

clue.text: Acting alone?

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: doing a deed without accomplices

explanation.surface: Someone doing a deed without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting alone' is what police say of a lone culprit; read as theatre, it is a solo performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre sense: a show with a single performer is acting alone in the literal sense.

clue.text: Help fool start to succeed in Congress

indicators.note: The start of a word is its first letter.
Being in something means sitting inside it.

explanation.surface: A plea for a clown to help get things going in the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress with a capital C looks like the US legislature; here it is sexual congress, which crosswords call 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to assist someone and to help them are the same act of lending a hand.

clue.text: Fragrant setting snubbed conference organiser

parts.note: SCENE, a setting, with its tail cut off
TED, the organisation behind TED Talks conferences

explanation.surface: An organiser who was snubbed at a conference venue.

explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something scented has a perfume, so it is fragrant.

clue.text: Italian side brought over English official to meddle

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club

clue.text: Attention-grabbing sound in extremely trite melody

clue.text: Arrogance of attitude worn by troublemakers more nakedly

clue.text: Very high key's what ends Callas, if you ask me

clue.text: Mass decree getting disorderly fellows the booze

clue.text: Strain to bite around seed in salad

clue.text: Short shirt covers ribs, but not guts?

clue.text: Trendy doll with rotating arm grasps bits of food

parts.note: to get an idea is to grasp it

explanation.surface: A fashionable action figure with a swivelling arm clutches some morsels.

clue.text: One might explain constant abuse of air rifle

parts.note: c, the speed of light, the classic constant

indicators.note: Abusing something means misusing it, twisting its letters out of their proper order.

explanation.surface: A warning about constant misuse of an air gun, and someone to explain it.

clue.text: Paint two beasts, one consuming second

clue.text: Finale turned into large-scale frenzy

indicators.note: Going into something means ending up inside it.

clue.text: Darling son, little man, tucking into pastry

clue.text: Was trumpeter paid to play clubs ultimately well trained?

clue.text: Stop rave taking over a university eatery
